    About
    I am a second-year PhD student in Biomedical Engineering at Johns Hopkins University and a member of the JEFworks Lab, advised by Dr. Jean Fan. My research focuses on computational methods for spatial transcriptomics, with an emphasis on modeling cell-cell communication within tissues. This work centers on developing open-source tools that researchers can readily apply to their own data.

title: Reflections as a graduate student
text: In this blog, I will share my thoughts and experiences as a graduate student at Johns Hopkins University. In an era of rapid expansion of the use of Large Language Models (LLMs), in research there is a growing question about the ability of these models to be able to conduct autonomous research. I had a conversation today with a fellow CCB member, and we discussed the feasibility of LLMs in this context, and we were not convinced that they can fully replace human researchers in the near future.
